tier_reason: README_AMD.md only describes optimizations (improved SIMD kernels, copy functions, 256-bit kernel selection, in-place MPI transpose, fast planner) with no numbers, and the releases page lists features without figures. AMD's own performance pages and the third-party pages found by search (openbenchmarking.org, AUR, dl.acm.org) are blocked here, so no measurement was seen.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 64 stars, 23 forks; AMD's official FFT library in AOCL (releases 3.0.1 through 5.3), packaged in Spack (amdfftw, versions up to 5.3) and AUR (fftw-amd)
corrections.caveats: Tier D: vendor claim with no numbers on any repository page (README_AMD.md, README, releases). AMD's benchmark pages (amd.com, docs.amd.com), openbenchmarking.org and the AUR page were blocked in this container. Search snippets (not opened) point both ways: an independent ICPP 2023 paper (GFFT, dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3605573.3605587) is summarised as finding AOCL-FFTW 'comparable' to FFTW in double-complex runs on EPYC, while another snippet of unknown origin reports about 30% over stock FFTW on a Ryzen 3700X; neither was verified. Code is derived from FFTW 3.3.10, but GitHub shows no 'forked from' parent, so is_fork_of stays null. COPYRIGHT gives GPL-2.0-or-later; GitHub labels it GPL-2.0; Spack lists GPL-2.0-only and links an AMD EULA for AOCL binaries; the NOTICES file also lists BSD-2-Clause notices for some FFTW 3.3.10 files. Recent releases (5.2, 5.3) say 'No major change'. Notable enough for a tier D entry as AMD's vendor build.

notes: No numbers anywhere reachable, so tier D stands; kept because it is AMD's official AOCL component (Spack and AUR packages), not rejected as not notable despite 64 stars. Shortcoming worth recording: an independent paper (via search snippet) is summarised as finding no clear gain over FFTW on EPYC. License refined to GPL-2.0-or-later from the COPYRIGHT file. Last commit 2026-05-19 (merge of the 5.3 release branch), active.
